'''Valerii Vinokur''' (also spelled as '''Vinokour''', or '''Valery Vinokour'''; 26 April 1949 — 16 December 2025<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/obituaries/valerii-m-vinokur|title=Valerii M. Vinokur|website=www.aip.org|date=27 April 2026 }}</ref>) was a [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] who worked on superconductivity, the physics of vortices, disordered media and glasses, nonequilibrium physics of dissipative systems, [[quantum phase transition]]s, quantum thermodynamics, and topological quantum matter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anl.gov/article/superinsulators-to-become-scientists-quark-playgrounds|title=Superinsulators to become scientists' quark playgrounds &#124; Argonne National Laboratory|website=www.anl.gov|date=30 January 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anl.gov/article/researchers-reverse-the-flow-of-time-on-ibms-quantum-computer|title=Researchers reverse the flow of time on IBM's quantum computer &#124; Argonne National Laboratory|website=www.anl.gov|date=13 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencealert.com/physicists-have-reversed-time-on-the-smallest-scale-with-a-quantum-computer|title=Physicists Have Reversed Time on The Smallest Scale Using a Quantum Computer|first=Mike|last=McRae|website=ScienceAlert|date=12 June 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/08/science/quantum-physics-time.html|title=For a Split Second, a Quantum Computer Made History Go Backward|first=Dennis|last=Overbye|newspaper=The New York Times|date=8 May 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2020-05-insight-reveals-topological-tangle-unexpected.html|title=Novel insight reveals topological tangle in unexpected corner of the universe|first=Savannah|last=Mitchem|website=Phys.Org, May 26, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2020-08-thermal-chaos-quantum-unknown.html|title=Thermal chaos returns quantum system to its unknown past|first=Nicolas|last=Posunko|website=Phys.Org, August 6, 2020}}</ref> He was a senior scientist and Argonne Distinguished Fellow at [[Argonne National Laboratory]] and a senior scientist at the Consortium for Advanced Science and Engineering, Office of Research and National Laboratories, The [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web|title = Vinokur's profile at ANL|url = https://www.anl.gov/profile/valerii-vinokour|access-date = 2020-07-02|archive-date = 2020-06-11|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200611213553/https://www.anl.gov/profile/valerii-vinokour|url-status = dead}}</ref> He was a Foreign Member of the National [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] and a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].

==Career==

Vinokur earned his BSc in physics of metals at [[Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys]] in 1972 and moved to the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Russia)|Institute of Solid State Physics]], [[Chernogolovka]], Russia, where he received a Ph.D. in physics in 1979. He has held appointments as a visiting scientist at [[CNRS]], Grenoble (1987), a visiting scientist at [[Leiden University]] (1989), a visiting scientist at [[ETH]] (Zurich) (1990), and as visiting director of research at [[Ecole Normale Superieure]] (Paris) (1996). Since 1990 till January 2021 Vinokur has worked at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]], having become a Distinguished Argonne Fellow in 2009.<ref name="auto"/> Since 2018 till January 2021, he has been a senior scientist at the Consortium for Advanced Science and Engineering, Office of Research and National Laboratories, The University of Chicago. Since January 2021 Vinokur has been working for Terra Quantum AG as a Chief Technology Officer US. Since January 2021 Vinokur also has been an adjunct professor at City College of the City University of New York.
